questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

The interviewer said, “Rajiv, I’m impressed with you

options.text: The interviewer told to Rajiv that he is impressed with him.
The interviewer said to Rajiv that he had been impressed with you.
The interviewer says I am impressed with Rajiv.
The interviewer told Rajiv that he was impressed with him.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 4.**
 
• While changing the given direct form of the sentence into its indirect form, 'said' will be changed to 'told' and will be joined by the conjunction 'that', 'is' will be changed to 'was'.
 
• Therefore, the correct structure is followed in option 4 i.e.** 'The interviewer told Rajiv that he was impressed with him.'**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

The old lady said, “May God bless you and give you all you desire in life!”

options.text: The old lady said that God may bless you and give you all you desire in life.
The old lady said that God will bless me and give me all I desire in life.
The old lady wished that God would bless me and give me all I desired in life.
The old lady says that may God bless you and give you all you desire in life.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option '**The old lady wished that God would bless me and give me all I desired in life.**'**

__
 
• The given direct form of the sentence is expressing a wish.
 
• While converting it into its indirect form, 'said' will be changed to 'wished' and will be joined by the conjunction that, 'may' will be changed to '', 'you' will be changed to 'me'.
 
• Therefore, the correct structure is followed in option 3 '**The old lady wished that God would bless me and give me all I desired in life**.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
• Option 1st is incorrect as 'wrong reported verb' is given i.e. The old lady said that God ***may*** bless
 
• Option 2 is incorrect as incorrect usage of verb** (will) **with incorrect verb given in Reported speech **(desire)**
 
• Option 4th is incorrect as incorrect usage of verb i.e.** (says)**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

‘Let’s not go out today. It’s going to be a hot day,” he said to me.

options.text: He is suggesting that they shouldn’t go out today as it was going to be a hot day.
He suggested that we shouldn’t be going out that day as it is going to be a hot day.
He suggested that we shouldn’t go out that day as it was going to be a hot day.
He had suggested that they shouldn’t go out today as it was going to be a hot day.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 3.**
 
• The word 'let us' in the given sentence shows that the sentence is expressing a suggestion.
 
• While converting it into its indirect form 'said to me' will be changed to 'suggested me', 'us' will be changed to 'we', 'is' will be changed to 'was'.
 
• Therefore, the correct structure is followed in option 3 i.e. '**He suggested that we shouldn’t go out that day as it was going to be a hot day.'**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

Rashmi says, “My startup is doing very well.”

options.text: Rashmi says that her startup is doing very well.
Rashmi says that my startup is doing very well.
Rashmi said that her startup was doing very well.
Rashmi said that her startup is doing very well.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 1.**
 
• The given direct form of the sentence is **an assertive sentence.**
 
• While changing it into its indirect form, **'says/said' remains unchanged**. '**comma**' and **'inverted commas' are removed **and is joined by the **conjunction **'**that**'.
 
• The possessive adjective '**my**' will be changed to '**her**'.
 
• Therefore, the correct structure is followed in option 1 i.e. **'Rashmi says that her startup is doing very well.'**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

“Don’t use your mobile while crossing the road,” I said to him.

options.text: I am advising him not to use his mobile while crossing the road.
I told him to not to use his mobile while crossing the road.
I said him not to use his mobile while crossing the road.
I advised him not to use his mobile while crossing the road.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 4.**
 
• The given sentence is in its direct form which is expressing a piece of advice.
 
• While converting it into its indirect form, 'I said to him' will be changed to 'I advised him', 'don't' will be changed to 'no to', second person 'your' will be changed to third person 'his'.
 
• Therefore, the correct structure is followed in option 4 i.e. **'I advised him not to use his mobile while crossing the road.'**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

The commander said, “Keep marching till you reach the border."

options.text: The commander requested the men keep marching till they reach the border.
The commander said to his men they should keep marching till you reach the border.
The commander ordered his men to keep marching till they reached the border.
The commander said the men should keep marching till they reach the border.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 3.**
 
• The reported speech in the given sentence is an **imperative sentence** and in the reporting speech 'commander' is mentioned.
 
• Hence, 'said' will be changed to '**ordered**' as 'commander' will give 'order' to his men.
 
• '**To**' will be used as a conjunction to join reporting and reported speech. 
 
• Out of given alternatives, these rules are followed only in option 3.
 
• Therefore, the correct indirect form of the given sentence is** 'The commander ordered his men to keep marching till they reached the border.'**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

"Why is everybody leaving so early today?" said the manager

options.text: The manager asked why was everybody leaving so early that day.
The manager asked why everybody was leaving so early today.
The manager asked why everybody left so early that day.
The manager asked why everybody was leaving so early that day

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 4.**
 
• While changing a sentence from direct form to indirect form the** present tense **in the reported speech is changed to **past tense**.
 
• Hence, '**is**' will be changed to '**was**'. 
 
• Interrogative sentence is changed to assertive or simple sentence, hence, was should be used after the subject 'everybody'.
 
• '**Today**' is changed to** 'that day'.**
 
• Out of given alternatives, these rules are followed only in option 4.
 
• Therefore, the correct indirect form of the given sentence is** 'The manager asked why everybody was leaving so early that day.'**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

The teacher suggested that the PTM be postponed to the third Saturday of the month.

options.text: The teacher said, “Let’s postpone the PTM to the third Saturday of the month."
The teacher suggested, “The PTM must be postponed to the third Saturday of the month.”
The teacher told, “The PTM will be postponed to the third Saturday of the month."
The teacher said, “The PTM would be postponed to the third Saturday of the month.”

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 1.**
 
• The use of word '**suggested**' in the reporting speech in the given sentence that the sentence in the reported speech should be a **proposal/suggestion**.
 
• '**Let's**' is used to show a **proposal/suggestion**, hence, it should be used in the reported speech.
 
• Out of given alternatives, 'let's' has been used only in option 1.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'The teacher said, **“Let’s postpone the PTM to the third Saturday of the month."'**

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to change the narration (direct / indirect) of the given sentence.

The salesgirl said, “Forgive me but this dress is already sold.”

options.text: The salesgirl begged forgiveness and regretted that the dress was already sold.
The salesgirl asked to be forgiven but this dress was already sold.
The salesgirl said to me to forgive her but this dress was sold.
The salesgirl said that she is sorry but this dress is already sold.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 1.**
 
• In the given sentence shows that the salesgirl is begging for forgiveness and feels sorry that the dress was already sold.
 
• While changing it into its indirect form, 'said' will be changed to 'begged', 'this' becomes 'that', 'is' becomes 'was'.
 
• Therefore, the correct indirect form of the sentence is **'The salesgirl begged forgiveness and regretted that the dress was already sold.'**
